headline: WFP cuts monthly food aid for 500,000 Gazans as funding collapses
dek: WFP will cut monthly food/cash assistance for 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza (reach falls 1.6M -> 1.1M) amid a funding shortfall; rations halved, cash aid cut for 75,000 families, daily hot meals 250,000 -> 150,000, every-other-day meals near the 'Yellow Line'; WFP needs $450M for six months; 1.4M…
sources: UN World Food Programme announcement; UN News (news.un.org); Reuters; AFP (country director Shaun Hughes quotes)
fault_line: Donor fatigue and broken pledges — vs — a 'ceasefire' under which Israel still kills daily and aid is strangled. Is the cut about money, or about a truce that was never real?

sections.what_happened: WFP will cut monthly food/cash assistance for 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza (reach falls 1.6M -> 1.1M) amid a funding shortfall; rations halved, cash aid cut for 75,000 families, daily hot meals 250,000 -> 150,000, every-other-day meals near the 'Yellow Line'; WFP needs $450M for six months; 1.4M Gazans (~2/3 of population) face crisis-level food insecurity, 200,000 in emergency conditions; acting ED Carl Skau visited Deir al-Balah soup kitchen Oct 18. West Bank aid already halved in September (400k -> 200k).
sections.what_verified: UN News story + Reuters reporting + AFP quotes of Hughes and Skau; consistent figures across Haaretz, Telegraph India, HinduBusinessLine, JPost (all wire-based).
sections.what_disputed: WFP frames cuts as funding-driven, not access-driven; critics note Israel's 'dual use' restrictions and daily ceasefire violations (per Guardian editorial/Anadolu: 1,522 killed since Oct 2025 truce) as the structural driver — the fault line, not a rebuttal of the numbers.
sections.why_matters: One year into the US-brokered Gaza ceasefire: 500,000 people lose their food aid this month — not to bombs but to an empty fund. The truce survives on paper; the kitchens close. Winter is four weeks away.
sections.context: Background: WFP cuts monthly food aid for 500,000 Gazans as funding collapses — NEW Monday

totw_analysis: Our read: One year into the US-brokered Gaza ceasefire: 500,000 people lose their food aid this month — not to bombs but to an empty fund. The truce survives on paper; the kitchens close. Winter is four weeks away. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Donor fatigue and broken pledges — vs — a 'ceasefire' under which Israel still kills daily and aid is strangled. Is the cut about money, or about a truce that was never real?
